newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal boosts three-year public investment budget.
newsitem.headline: Senegal boosts three-year public investment budget.

text.p: Senegal on Thursday estimated its public investment budget for the 1997-99 plan at 7.963 billion CFA francs and said most of the financing had been secured.
Economy Minister Pape Ousmane Sacko told the country's Social and Economic Council that the public investment budget represented an eight percent rise over the previous plan.
He said 71.5 percent or 620.446 billion CFA had already been secured for a total of 341 projects under the plan. Foreign funding would account for 68 percent of the budget.

Replying to a question on Senegal's debt during the public hearing, the minister said foreign debt was not a problem for Senegal because it amounted to 75 percent of Gross Domestic Product, against an Africa average of 110 percent of GDP.
Senegal's debt is officially put at 1,700 billion CFA.
